libs.note: BH-6374. Sibling parts of one split slice (a parent's DECOMPOSED children, such as TK-184 and TK-185, or dotted keys such as TK-142.1) whose pre-plan file lists share a path run one at a time, in n order, and a part with no list waits for a sibling in flight. bin/fly-pool.sh:pool_spawn_decision gate 0c runs `bin/sibling-serial.sh check` and keeps the row queued on rc 3, logging `SIBLING_SERIAL <K> waits for <S> on <file>` to logs/fly-pool.log. bin/overlap-schedule.sh runs `decide` and prints the verdict as a HELD line. lane_switch sibling-serial-off is the same kill switch as SIBLING_SERIAL=0.

knobs.note: 1 = the pool holds a sibling part behind a colliding sibling. 0 (or off) = check answers go for every key and the pool spawns as before. Read by bin/sibling-serial.sh check as _preplan_env SIBLING_SERIAL 1 after lib_env_apply sibling-serial.
A lower-n queued sibling whose enqueued_at is older than this holds nobody: it is stuck for another reason (HOLD, a cap), and one stderr line in logs/fly-pool.log says so.

The wait ceiling, timed from state/sibling-serial/

/.sibling-since. At the ceiling the key is released, SIBLING_SERIAL_RELEASED is logged, and one warn alert is sent per (key, blocker). Equal to POOL_AFTER_MAX_MIN by default.
